rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes please, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — that means a lot, and five hours a week of a data analyst's time is exactly the kind of help Halcyon Threshold needs. Here's the concrete thing I'd love to start with: a public, well-sourced tracker of frontier AI labs' safety commitments. Labs publish safety frameworks, responsible scaling policies, and incident/eval commitments — but nobody maintains a clean, neutral dataset of (a) what exactly was promised, (b) when, (c) what evidence exists that it's being followed, with citations for every cell. It's neglected, it's genuinely useful to researchers and journalists, and it plays to writing + data skills rather than requiring lab access. A possible first iteration, sized to ~5 hrs/week: 1. Week 1–2: pick 4–6 major labs, collect their published safety policy documents, and build a simple schema (commitment, source URL, date, category, verifiable? y/n). 2. Week 3–4: fill it in for one lab end-to-end as a template, then we review together and decide format (spreadsheet vs. small website table). If that sounds dull or you'd rather do something else (there's also a regulatory public-comment docket closing 20 Nov that could use an analyst's eye), say so — I'd rather match the work to what you'll enjoy. Want to pick a 30-minute slot this week to scope it? Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold (sent by Morgan's assistant on Morgan's behalf)"
rows.quote: **Priya Raman** — accepted her offer, proposed the tracker as her first task + a scoping call.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I have to pass on an attributed quote for now — I'm not in a position to be quoted by name in press at the moment, for boring employment-paperwork reasons rather than anything interesting. Two things I can offer instead: - If it helps your piece, the project's framing is simple and you're welcome to describe it in general terms: Halcyon Threshold is a small independent effort premised on the idea that the arrival of superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens, and that making it go well deserves far more hands than it currently has — including people outside the big labs. (Please don't attribute that to me by name.) - I'd genuinely like to talk once my situation is sorted, likely in a few weeks. If you're writing follow-ups, I'm happy to be on your list. Good luck with the deadline, Morgan (sent by Morgan's assistant on Morgan's behalf)"
rows.quote: **declined Tessa Brandt's named quote**, offering unattributed framing and future contact instead
